subject: Post-call recap: PayFlux discovery — tool calls & structured/output requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@payflux.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: PayFlux discovery — tool calls & structured/output requirements

Hi Liam — thanks for the 30-minute intro earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll update.

Key pain points you shared
- Reconciliation pipeline frequently fails due to inconsistent outputs from current NLU layer (missing fields / date formats).
- Internal API "post_transaction" needs exactly-typed JSON; downstream systems reject nonconforming messages.
- Current latency spikes during peak settlement windows (batch processing) cause timeouts.

Current stack you mentioned
- Kubernetes-hosted microservices, in-house NLU for intent extraction, Kafka-based event mesh, downstream accounting service that enforces a strict JSON schema.

Success criteria we captured
- Generated outputs must validate against a canonical JSON schema (schema-level validation >=99.5% on a 10k sample).
- Deterministic, machine-parseable responses: stable field presence and consistent formats (ISO8601 UTC timestamps, cents as integers, currency codes standardized).
- Latency SLO: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms for per-request end-to-end generation (before any network hops to post_transaction).

Redwood capabilities relevant to this ask
- Function/tool calling: model -> structured payload that can be routed to your post_transaction API (we can simulate the call during POC).
- JSON schema handshake: we can validate outputs on the server-side and fall back to guarded variants if validation fails.
- Dedicated & Private deployment options if you need VPC/on-prem isolation.

Proposed next steps
1) You share a small set of representative payloads and the canonical schema (1–2 business days).
2) We prepare a short eval plan (I attached a draft: proposed-eval-plan.md) that runs 1k–3k sample generations and returns validation metrics.
3) Tech deep-dive (60 min) to map function wiring and network egress requirements — can your engineering lead take this next week?
4) Procurement: we’ll surface a short SOW/term sheet once we align on scope. I attached our PSA for reference (redwood-psa.pdf).

Attachments: redwood-psa.pdf (PSA stub), proposed-eval-plan.md (draft).

Thanks again — available tomorrow afternoon for the deep dive if that works.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PayFlux discovery — tool calls & structured/output requirements

Thanks Rafael — this is a clean summary, appreciate it. A few clarifications and a sample payload attached.

Clarifications from our side
- Validation bar: we need schema validation on every generated message before it hits our accounting service. Prefer automatic rejection/fallback rather than corrected guesses.
- Function call: model needs to return a deterministic JSON body that maps 1:1 to our post_transaction API signature (fields: transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, source_account, timestamp_iso, merchant_id, metadata).
- Privacy/regulatory: we prefer a VPC-hosted control plane for PII controls; we can discuss SOC2 and retention during procurement.

Traffic & scale
- Peak: expected 400 rps during settlement windows (bursty). Monthly token estimate: ~10M tokens.
- For POC, a smaller slice (50–100 rps) is fine.

Procurement contact
- Eileen Park (eileen.park@payflux.com) handles SOW and PO. I’m looping her on next messages.

Attached: sample-payloads.json (10 examples).

I can do the technical deep dive on Thursday 8/6 at 11:00am ET.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, PayFlux
liam.o@payflux.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PayFlux discovery — tool calls & structured/output requirements

Liam — great, thanks for the details and the sample payloads. Confirming the Thursday slot for the technical deep-dive (I’ll send a calendar invite).

Short technical plan for Thursday (what we’ll cover)
- Schema handshake: we’ll propose a canonical JSON schema (example below) and show the server-side validation enforcement.
- Function call wiring: how Redwood surfaces a function-like response (JSON body + metadata) so you can route directly to post_transaction or inspect before POST.
- Failure modes & fallbacks: automatic 'validation_failed' variants, policy for retries, and logging/audit for rejected messages.
- Performance baseline: expected p50/p95 with sample tokens and options for batching/kv-cache tuning.

Example canonical schema (illustrative):
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["transaction_id","amount_cents","currency","source_account","timestamp_iso","merchant_id"],
  "properties": {
    "transaction_id": {"type":"string"},
    "amount_cents": {"type":"integer"},
    "currency": {"type":"string","minLength":3,"maxLength":3},
    "source_account": {"type":"string"},
    "timestamp_iso": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
    "merchant_id": {"type":"string"},
    "metadata": {"type":"object"}
  }
}

Deterministic formatting definition we’ll use for the eval
- Field presence: required fields must be present and non-null.
- Type stability: types must match schema (no strings where ints are declared).
- Canonical timestamp format: ISO8601 in UTC.
- No extra top-level keys allowed for the strict eval (we can allow optional metadata under a single 'metadata' object).

Proposed POC (2 weeks)
- Week 1: deploy a sandbox Dedicated instance, run 1k–5k sample generations, measure schema pass-rate and latency.
- Week 2: integrate function-call wiring to a staging post_transaction endpoint; run end-to-end validation and failure handling.

Can you confirm the staging endpoint for post_transaction and whether we can get a short sample dataset (10k rows is ideal but 1k is workable)? Also confirm Eileen as procurement contact and any NX terms we should anticipate.

Attachments: proposed-eval-plan.md (updated draft). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
